title.zh: 卷52 列傳第17 韓擒虎 賀若弼
title.en: Volume 52 Biographies 17: Han Qinhu, He Ruobi
title.raw: 卷52 列傳第17 韓擒虎 賀若弼 Volume 52 Biographies 17: Han Qinhu, He Ruobi

sentences.zh: 隋書卷五十二列傳第十七

translations.literal: Book of Sui, Volume 52, Biographies 17
translations.idiomatic: Book of Sui, Volume 52, Biographies 17

sentences.zh: ○韓擒虎弟僧壽洪

translations.literal: ○ Han Qinhu; his brothers Sengshou and Hong
translations.idiomatic: ○ Han Qinhu; his brothers Sengshou and Hong

sentences.zh: 韓擒虎，字子通，河南東垣人也，後家新安。

translations.literal: Han Qinhu, courtesy name Zitong, was a native of Dongyuan in Henan; his family later settled in Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qinhu, whose courtesy name was Zitong, came from Dongyuan in Henan and later made his home in Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 父雄，以武烈知名，仕周，官至大將軍、洛虞等八州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Xiong was famed for martial valor; he served Zhou and rose to Grand General and governor of eight prefectures including Luo and Yu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Han Xiong won renown for martial prowess, served the Northern Zhou, and eventually reached the rank of Grand General while holding eight prefectures, among them Luo and Yu.

sentences.zh: 擒虎少慷慨，以膽略見稱，容貌魁岸，有雄傑之表。

translations.literal: In youth Qinhu was open-handed and bold, famed for courage and stratagem; his features were towering, with the bearing of a hero.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man Qinhu was generous and daring, celebrated for nerve and strategy, with a towering frame and the look of a born champion.

sentences.zh: 性又好書，經史百家皆略知大旨。

translations.literal: He also loved books and had a rough grasp of the main themes of the classics, histories, and the hundred schools.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning too and had a working grasp of the essentials of the classics, histories, and the hundred schools.

sentences.zh: 周太祖見而異之，令與諸子遊集。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu of Zhou saw him and was struck by him, and had him join in gatherings with his sons.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Taizu saw him he took him for remarkable and had him keep company with the imperial princes.

sentences.zh: 後以軍功，拜都督、新安太守，稍遷儀同三司，襲爵新義郡公。

translations.literal: Later, for military merit, he was appointed Area Commander and Administrator of Xin'an, then gradually promoted to Yitong Third Rank and inherited the title Duke of Xinyi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Later, on account of battlefield merit, he was made area commander and Administrator of Xin'an, then gradually promoted to Yitong Third Rank and succeeded to the title Duke of Xinyi.

sentences.zh: 武帝伐齊，齊將獨孤永業守金墉城，擒虎說下之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu attacked Qi, the Qi general Dugu Yongye held Jinyong city; Qinhu talked him into surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu campaigned against Qi, the Qi commander Dugu Yongye held Jinyong; Qinhu persuaded him to submit.

sentences.zh: 進平范陽，加上儀同，拜永州刺史。

translations.literal: Advancing, he pacified Fanyang, was given additional Yitong rank, and appointed Administrator of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to pacify Fanyang, received an additional Yitong rank, and was appointed Administrator of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 陳人逼光州，擒虎以行軍總管擊破之。

translations.literal: When Chen forces pressed Guangzhou, Qinhu as campaigning commander defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen troops pressed Guangzhou, Qinhu, serving as campaigning commander, routed them.

sentences.zh: 又從宇文忻平合州。

translations.literal: He also followed Yuwen Xin in pacifying Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He also followed Yuwen Xin in bringing Hezhou to submission.

sentences.zh: 高祖作相，遷和州刺史。

translations.literal: When Gaozu became Chancellor, Qinhu was moved to Administrator of Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took power as Chancellor, Qinhu was transferred to Administrator of Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 陳將甄慶、任蠻奴、蕭摩訶等共為聲援，頻寇江北，前後入界。

translations.literal: Chen generals Zhen Qing, Ren Mannu, Xiao Mohe and others gave mutual support and repeatedly raided north of the Yangtze, crossing the border again and again.
translations.idiomatic: Chen commanders Zhen Qing, Ren Mannu, Xiao Mohe, and others backed one another and raided the north bank of the Yangtze time and again.

sentences.zh: 擒虎屢挫其鋒，陳人奪氣。

translations.literal: Qinhu repeatedly blunted their edge, and the Chen lost heart.
translations.idiomatic: Qinhu repeatedly broke their momentum until the Chen lost their fighting spirit.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，高祖潛有吞併江南之志，以擒虎有文武才用，夙著聲名，於是拜為廬州總管，委以平陳之任，甚為敵人所憚。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang, Gaozu secretly cherished the aim of swallowing the south, and because Qinhu had both civil and military talent and long-standing fame, he was appointed Commander-in-Chief of Luzhou and entrusted with the task of pacifying Chen, greatly feared by the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaihuang era Gaozu quietly aimed to absorb the south. Seeing that Qinhu combined civil and military gifts with a reputation already established, he appointed him Commander-in-Chief of Luzhou and entrusted him with the conquest of Chen—a man the enemy deeply dreaded.

sentences.zh: 及大舉伐陳，以擒虎為先鋒。

translations.literal: When the great campaign against Chen was launched, Qinhu was made vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: When the great assault on Chen was mounted, Qinhu was made vanguard.

sentences.zh: 擒虎率五百人宵濟，襲採石，守者皆醉，擒虎遂取之。

translations.literal: Qinhu led five hundred men across by night, struck Caishi; the defenders were all drunk, and Qinhu took it.
translations.idiomatic: Qinhu led five hundred men across the river by night and struck Caishi; the garrison was drunk, and he seized the place.

sentences.zh: 進攻姑熟，半日而拔，次於新林。

translations.literal: He attacked Gushu and took it in half a day, then encamped at Xinlin.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed Gushu and captured it within half a day, then halted at Xinlin.

sentences.zh: 江南父老素聞其威信，來謁軍門，晝夜不絕。

translations.literal: The elders of the south had long heard of his prestige and trustworthiness and came to his camp gate day and night without cease.
translations.idiomatic: The elders of Jiangnan, who had long known his authority and good faith, came to his camp day and night without pause.

sentences.zh: 陳人大駭，其將樊巡、魯世真、田瑞等相繼降之。

translations.literal: The Chen were greatly alarmed; their generals Fan Xun, Lu Shizhen, Tian Rui and others surrendered to him in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The Chen were thrown into panic; their officers Fan Xun, Lu Shizhen, Tian Rui, and others submitted to him one after another.

sentences.zh: 晉王廣上狀，高祖聞而大悅，宴賜群臣。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin Yang Guang reported upward; Gaozu heard and was greatly pleased and feasted and rewarded the ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin, Yang Guang, sent a memorial; when Gaozu heard the news he was delighted and gave a feast to reward his ministers.

sentences.zh: 晉王遣行軍總管杜彥與擒虎合軍，步騎二萬，陳叔寶遣領軍蔡徵守朱雀航，聞擒虎將至，眾懼而潰。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin sent the campaigning commander Du Yan to join forces with Qinhu—twenty thousand foot and horse. Chen Shubao sent the Director of the Palace Guard Cai Zheng to hold the Zhuque crossing; when they heard Qinhu was coming the troops were afraid and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin sent the campaigning commander Du Yan to unite with Qinhu at the head of twenty thousand infantry and cavalry. Chen Shubao sent the Director of the Palace Guard Cai Zheng to hold the Zhuque ford; when the army heard Qinhu was approaching, fear broke their ranks and they fled.

sentences.zh: 任蠻奴為賀若弼所敗，棄軍降於擒虎。

translations.literal: Ren Mannu had been defeated by He Ruobi and abandoned his army to surrender to Qinhu.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Mannu, already beaten by He Ruobi, cast off his force and surrendered to Qinhu.

sentences.zh: 擒虎以精騎五百，直入硃雀門。

translations.literal: Qinhu with five hundred picked horsemen entered straight through the Zhuque Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Qinhu entered the Zhuque Gate at the head of five hundred elite horsemen.

sentences.zh: 陳人欲戰，蠻奴捴之曰：「老夫尚降，諸君何事！

translations.literal: The Chen wished to fight; Mannu restrained them, saying: "This old man has already surrendered—what business have you gentlemen!"
translations.idiomatic: The Chen wanted to fight, but Mannu held them back, saying, "Even I, an old man, have submitted—what are you still fighting for!"

sentences.zh: 」眾皆散走。

translations.literal: " The crowd all scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The troops all broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 遂平金陵，執陳主叔寶。

translations.literal: He then pacified Jinling and seized the Chen ruler Shubao.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon pacified Jinling and took the Chen ruler Shubao prisoner.

sentences.zh: 時賀若弼亦有功。

translations.literal: At the time He Ruobi also had merit.
translations.idiomatic: He Ruobi had won merit as well.

sentences.zh: 乃下詔于晉王曰：「此二公者，深謀大略，東南逋寇，朕本委之，靜地恤民，悉如朕意。

translations.literal: An edict was then issued to the Prince of Jin: "These two lords possess deep strategy and broad design. The fugitive bandits of the southeast I originally entrusted to them; in calming the land and cherishing the people they have done entirely as I wished.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent an edict to the Prince of Jin: "These two men possess deep strategy and grand design. The fugitive rebels of the southeast I originally entrusted to them; in quieting the realm and caring for the people they have acted wholly as I wished.

sentences.zh: 九州不一，已數百年，以名臣之功，成太平之業，天下盛事，何用過此！

translations.literal: The Nine Provinces have not been one for several hundred years; through the merit of famed ministers a peaceful age is achieved—what event under heaven surpasses this!"
translations.idiomatic: For centuries the realm has not been united; through the service of great ministers a peaceful order is won—what triumph under heaven could exceed this!"

sentences.zh: 聞以欣然，實深慶快。

translations.literal: Hearing it I am pleased; my joy is deep indeed.
translations.idiomatic: To hear of it fills me with pleasure; my delight is profound.

sentences.zh: 平定江表，二人之力也。

translations.literal: The pacification of the lands south of the Yangtze is the work of these two men.
translations.idiomatic: The pacification of Jiangbiao is the achievement of these two men.

sentences.zh: 」賜物萬段。

translations.literal: " Gifts of ten thousand bolts were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: He bestowed gifts of ten thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 又下優詔於擒虎、弼曰：「申國威于萬里，宣朝化於一隅，使東南之民俱出湯火，數百年寇旬日廓清，專是公之功也。

translations.literal: A gracious edict was also issued to Qinhu and Bi: "You have displayed the state's might for ten thousand li and spread the court's transforming influence in a corner of the realm, bringing the people of the southeast all out of boiling water and burning fire; bandits of centuries were cleared in a matter of days—this is your merit alone.
translations.idiomatic: Another gracious edict went to Qinhu and Bi: "You have proclaimed our might across ten thousand li and spread the court's civilizing influence in a distant quarter, lifting the people of the southeast out of fire and flood; centuries of marauding were swept away in days—this is your work alone.

sentences.zh: 高名塞于宇宙，盛業光於天壤，逖聽前古，罕聞其匹。

translations.literal: Your lofty names fill heaven and earth; your splendid achievements shine upon the sky and soil; listening back through antiquity, one rarely hears their equal.
translations.idiomatic: Your great names fill the cosmos; your splendid deeds light heaven and earth; searching the past, one seldom hears their like.

sentences.zh: 班師凱入，誠知非遠，相思之甚，寸陰若歲。

translations.literal: Your triumphant return cannot be far; my longing for you is so keen that each inch of shadow seems a year.
translations.idiomatic: Your victorious return cannot be far off; I miss you so keenly that every inch of shadow feels like a year.

sentences.zh: 」及至京，弼與擒虎爭功於上前，弼曰：「臣在蔣山死戰，破其銳卒，擒其驍將，震揚威武，遂平陳國。

translations.literal: " When they reached the capital, Bi and Qinhu disputed merit before the throne. Bi said: "Your servant fought to the death on Mount Jiang, broke their crack troops, seized their fierce generals, shook forth martial glory, and thus pacified the Chen state.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached the capital, Bi and Qinhu disputed their merits before the throne. Bi said, "Your servant fought to the death on Mount Jiang, broke their elite troops, captured their fiercest commanders, displayed martial might, and thereby pacified Chen.

sentences.zh: 韓擒虎略不交陣，豈臣之比！

translations.literal: Han Qinhu scarcely crossed spears with the enemy—how can he be compared with your servant!"
translations.idiomatic: Han Qinhu barely engaged the enemy in battle—how can he be compared with your servant!"

sentences.zh: 」擒虎曰：「本奉明旨，令臣與弼同時合勢，以取偽都。

translations.literal: Qinhu said: "I originally received the clear command that your servant and Bi should unite our strength at the same time to take the false capital.
translations.idiomatic: Qinhu said, "I originally received the explicit order that your servant and Bi should combine our forces at the same moment to seize the false capital.

sentences.zh: 弼乃敢先期，逢賊遂戰，致令將士傷死甚多。

translations.literal: Yet Bi dared to move ahead of schedule, met the enemy and fought, causing many officers and men to be wounded and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Bi dared to act early, met the enemy and gave battle, and caused a great many officers and men to be wounded or killed.

sentences.zh: 臣以輕騎五百，兵不血刃，直取金陵，降任蠻奴，執陳叔寶，據其府庫，傾其巢穴。

translations.literal: Your servant with five hundred light horsemen, without staining our blades, went straight to Jinling, made Ren Mannu submit, seized Chen Shubao, occupied their treasuries, and overturned their nest.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant, with five hundred light horsemen and without drawing blood from our blades, went straight to Jinling, received Ren Mannu's surrender, seized Chen Shubao, took their treasuries, and overturned their lair.

sentences.zh: 弼至夕，方扣北掖門，臣啟關而納之。

translations.literal: Bi did not reach until evening before he knocked at the North Yeta Gate; your servant opened the gate and admitted him.
translations.idiomatic: Bi did not arrive until evening, when he knocked at the North Yeta Gate; your servant opened the gate and let him in.

sentences.zh: 斯乃救罪不暇，安得與臣相比！

translations.literal: He had barely time to answer for his faults—how could he be compared with your servant!"
translations.idiomatic: He scarcely had time to answer for his offenses—how could he be compared with your servant!"

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「二將俱合上勳。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Both generals alike merit supreme merit."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Both generals alike deserve supreme merit."

sentences.zh: 」於是進位上柱國，賜物八千段。

translations.literal: " He was then advanced to Supreme Pillar of State and given eight thousand bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: He was then promoted to Supreme Pillar of State and given eight thousand bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 有司劾擒虎放縱士卒，淫汙陳宮，坐此不加爵邑。

translations.literal: The authorities impeached Qinhu for letting his soldiers run wild and defiling the Chen palace; for this he received no added fief or estate.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities impeached Qinhu for allowing his troops to run loose and defile the Chen palace; for this he received no added fief or estate.

sentences.zh: 先是，江東有謠歌曰：「黃斑青驄馬，發自壽陽涘。

translations.literal: Earlier, in Jiangdong there was a ballad that said: "Yellow spots on a blue piebald horse, setting out from the banks of Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in Jiangdong, there was a ballad that ran: "A piebald horse with yellow spots, setting out from the banks of Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 來時冬氣末，去日春風始。

translations.literal: Coming at winter's end, going when the spring wind begins."
translations.idiomatic: Arriving as winter wanes, departing when the spring wind rises."

sentences.zh: 」皆不知所謂。

translations.literal: " No one knew what it meant.
translations.idiomatic: No one knew what it meant.

sentences.zh: 擒虎本名豹，平陳之際，又乘青驄馬，往反時節與歌相應，至是方悟。

translations.literal: Qinhu's original name was Bao; at the time of pacifying Chen he again rode a blue piebald horse, and the seasons of his coming and going matched the song—only then did people understand.
translations.idiomatic: Qinhu's original name was Bao; during the pacification of Chen he again rode a blue piebald horse, and the seasons of his coming and going matched the song—only then did people understand.

sentences.zh: 其後突厥來朝，上謂之曰：「汝聞江南有陳國天子乎？

translations.literal: Later, when the Turks came to court, the emperor said to them: "Have you heard of the Son of Heaven of Chen in the south?"
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the Turks came to court, the emperor said to them, "Have you heard of the Son of Heaven of Chen in the south?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「聞之。

translations.literal: " They answered: "We have heard."
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "We have."

sentences.zh: 」上命左右引突厥詣擒虎前，曰：「此是執得陳國天子者。

translations.literal: " The emperor ordered attendants to lead the Turks before Qinhu and said: "This is the man who captured the Son of Heaven of Chen."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered attendants to lead the Turks before Qinhu and said, "This is the man who captured the Son of Heaven of Chen."

sentences.zh: 」擒虎厲然顧之，突厥惶恐，不敢仰視，其有威容如此。

translations.literal: " Qinhu glared at them sternly; the Turks were terrified and dared not look up—such was his imposing presence.
translations.idiomatic: Qinhu turned on them with a fierce look; the Turks were terrified and dared not raise their eyes—such was the force of his bearing.

sentences.zh: 別封壽光縣公，食邑千戶。

translations.literal: He was separately enfeoffed Duke of Shouguang county with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was separately enfeoffed Duke of Shouguang with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 以行軍總管屯金城，禦備胡寇，即拜涼州總管。

translations.literal: As campaigning commander he was stationed at Jincheng to guard against the Hu raiders and was at once appointed Commander-in-Chief of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: As campaigning commander he was posted at Jincheng to guard against northern raiders and was immediately appointed Commander-in-Chief of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 俄征還京，上宴之內殿，恩禮殊厚。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned back to the capital; the emperor feasted him in the inner hall with exceptional favor.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was recalled to the capital; the emperor feasted him in the inner hall with exceptional kindness.

sentences.zh: 無何，其鄰母見擒虎門下儀衛甚盛，有同王者，母異而問之。

translations.literal: Before long, a neighbor woman saw under Qinhu's gate a guard of honor as grand as a king's; the woman was startled and asked about it.
translations.idiomatic: Before long a neighbor woman saw at Qinhu's gate an escort as splendid as a king's; astonished, she asked what it meant.

sentences.zh: 其中人曰：「我來迎王。

translations.literal: One of the party said: "I have come to welcome the king."
translations.idiomatic: Someone in the party said, "I have come to welcome the king."

sentences.zh: 」忽然不見。

translations.literal: " Suddenly they vanished.
translations.idiomatic: Then they vanished.

sentences.zh: 又有人疾篤，忽驚走至擒虎家曰：「我欲謁王。

translations.literal: Another man, gravely ill, suddenly ran in alarm to Qinhu's house and said: "I wish to pay court to the king."
translations.idiomatic: Another man, desperately ill, suddenly ran in alarm to Qinhu's house and said, "I wish to pay court to the king."

sentences.zh: 」左右問曰：「何王也？

translations.literal: " His attendants asked: "What king?"
translations.idiomatic: His attendants asked, "Which king?"

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「閻羅王。

translations.literal: " He answered: "King Yama."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "King Yama."

sentences.zh: 」擒虎子弟欲撻之，擒虎止之曰：「生為上柱國，死作閻羅王，斯亦足矣。

translations.literal: " Qinhu's sons and nephews wished to beat him, but Qinhu stopped them, saying: "Alive I was a Supreme Pillar of State; dead I shall be King Yama—that is enough."
translations.idiomatic: Qinhu's sons and nephews wanted to thrash him, but Qinhu stopped them, saying, "Alive I was a Supreme Pillar of State; dead I shall be King Yama—that is enough."

sentences.zh: 」因寢疾，數日竟卒，時年五十五。

translations.literal: " He then took to his bed with illness and within days died, aged fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He then fell ill and within a few days died, at the age of fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 子世諤嗣。

translations.literal: His son Shiyu succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shiyu succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 世諤倜儻驍捷，有父風。

translations.literal: Shiyu was free-spirited, bold, and swift, with his father's manner.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyu was dashing, fierce, and quick, with his father's spirit.

sentences.zh: 楊玄感之作亂也，引世諤為將，每戰先登。

translations.literal: When Yang Xuangan rebelled, he recruited Shiyu as a commander; in every battle Shiyu led the charge.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Xuangan rose in rebellion he took Shiyu as a commander; in every battle Shiyu led the assault.

sentences.zh: 及玄感敗，為吏所拘。

translations.literal: When Xuangan was defeated, Shiyu was seized by the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuangan was defeated, Shiyu was seized by the authorities.

sentences.zh: 時帝在高陽，送詣行所。

translations.literal: The emperor was then at Gaoyang; Shiyu was sent to the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then at Gaoyang; Shiyu was sent to the traveling court.

sentences.zh: 世諤曰令守者市酒殽以酣暢，揚言曰：「吾死在朝夕，不醉何為！

translations.literal: Shiyu had the guards buy wine and food for a hearty feast and declared aloud: "I shall die any day now—if I do not get drunk, what is the use!"
translations.idiomatic: Shiyu had the guards buy wine and food for a hearty feast and cried aloud, "I shall die any day now—if I do not get drunk, what is the point!"

sentences.zh: 」漸以酒進守者，守者狎之，遂飲令致醉。

translations.literal: " Gradually he offered wine to the guards; they grew familiar with him and drank until he made them drunk.
translations.idiomatic: Little by little he pressed wine on the guards; they grew familiar with him and drank until he had made them drunk.

sentences.zh: 世諤因得逃奔山賊，不知所終。

translations.literal: Shiyu thus escaped and fled to mountain bandits; his end is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyu thus escaped and fled to mountain bandits; nothing more is known of his fate.

sentences.zh: 僧壽字玄慶，擒虎母弟也，亦以勇烈知名。

translations.literal: Sengshou, courtesy name Xuanqing, was Qinhu's younger brother by the same mother and was also famed for fierce valor.
translations.idiomatic: Sengshou, whose courtesy name was Xuanqing, was Qinhu's younger uterine brother and was likewise famed for fierce valor.

sentences.zh: 周武帝時，為侍伯中旅下大夫。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Wu of Zhou he was a lower grand master in the Central Brigade of the Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu of Zhou he served as a lower grand master in the Central Brigade of the Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 高祖得政，從韋孝寬平尉迥，每戰有功，授大將軍，封昌樂公，邑千戶。

translations.literal: When Gaozu seized power, he followed Wei Xiaokuan in pacifying Yu Chi Jiong's rebellion; in every battle he had merit and was made Grand General, enfeoffed Duke of Changle with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took power he followed Wei Xiaokuan in putting down Yu Chi Jiong; in every battle he distinguished himself and was made Grand General and enfeoffed Duke of Changle with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，拜安州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang he was appointed Administrator of Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Kaihuang he was appointed Administrator of Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 時擒虎為廬州總管，朝廷不欲同在淮南，轉為熊州刺史。

translations.literal: At that time Qinhu was Commander-in-Chief of Luzhou; the court did not wish the two brothers together in Huainan, so Sengshou was transferred to Administrator of Xiongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Qinhu was Commander-in-Chief of Luzhou; the court did not want both brothers in Huainan, so Sengshou was moved to Administrator of Xiongzhou.

sentences.zh: 後轉蔚州刺史，進爵廣陵郡公。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Administrator of Yu prefecture and advanced to Duke of Guangling commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was transferred to Administrator of Yu prefecture and advanced to Duke of Guangling.

sentences.zh: 尋以行軍總管擊突厥于雞頭山，破之。

translations.literal: Soon, as campaigning commander, he attacked the Turks at Mount Jitou and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, as campaigning commander, he struck the Turks at Mount Jitou and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 後坐事免。

translations.literal: Later he was dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 數歲，複拜蔚州刺史。

translations.literal: Several years later he was again appointed Administrator of Yu prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was again appointed Administrator of Yu prefecture.

sentences.zh: 突厥甚憚之。

translations.literal: The Turks greatly feared him.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks greatly feared him.

sentences.zh: 十七年，屯蘭州以備胡。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was stationed at Lanzhou to guard against the Hu.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was posted at Lanzhou to guard against northern peoples.

sentences.zh: 明年，遼東之役，領行軍總管，還，檢校靈州總管事。

translations.literal: The next year, in the Liaodong campaign, he led as campaigning commander; on his return he acted as inspector of the affairs of the Commander-in-Chief of Lingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, in the Liaodong campaign, he served as campaigning commander; on his return he acted as inspector of the affairs of the Commander-in-Chief of Lingzhou.

sentences.zh: 從楊素擊突厥，破之，進位上柱國，改封江都郡公。

translations.literal: Following Yang Su he struck the Turks and defeated them, was advanced to Supreme Pillar of State, and his fief was changed to Duke of Jiangdu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Following Yang Su he attacked the Turks and defeated them, was promoted to Supreme Pillar of State, and his fief was changed to Duke of Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，又改封新蔡郡公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded, his fief was again changed to Duke of Xincai commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded, his fief was again changed to Duke of Xincai.

sentences.zh: 自是之後，不復任用。

translations.literal: From then on he was no longer employed.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he was no longer employed.

sentences.zh: 大業五年，從幸太原。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Daye he followed the emperor to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Daye he accompanied the emperor to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 有京兆人達奚通妾王氏，能清歌，朝臣多相會觀之，僧壽亦豫焉，坐是除名。

translations.literal: A concubine of Daxi Tong of Jingzhao named Wang could sing clearly; many courtiers gathered to watch her, and Sengshou was among them; for this he was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: A concubine of Daxi Tong of Jingzhao named Wang could sing beautifully; many courtiers gathered to watch her, and Sengshou was among them; for this he was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 尋令復位。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered restored to his post.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was ordered restored to his post.

sentences.zh: 八年，卒于京師，時年六十五。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he died in the capital, aged sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he died in the capital, aged sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 有子孝基。

translations.literal: He had a son Xiaoji.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son Xiaoji.

sentences.zh: 洪字叔明，擒虎季弟也。

translations.literal: Hong, courtesy name Shuming, was Qinhu's youngest brother.
translations.idiomatic: Hong, whose courtesy name was Shuming, was Qinhu's youngest brother.

sentences.zh: 少驍勇，善射，膂力過人。

translations.literal: In youth he was fierce and brave, skilled at archery, with strength surpassing other men.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was fierce and brave, skilled at archery, with strength beyond ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 仕周侍伯上士，後以軍功拜大都督。

translations.literal: He served Zhou as a senior gentleman of the Palace Guard and later, for military merit, was appointed Grand Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He served Zhou as a senior gentleman of the Palace Guard and later, for military merit, was appointed Grand Commander.

sentences.zh: 高祖為丞相，從韋孝寬破尉迥於相州，加上開府，甘棠縣侯，邑八百戶。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was Chancellor, he followed Wei Xiaokuan in defeating Yu Chi Jiong at Xiangzhou, was given the rank of Upper Opening Master, made Marquis of Gantang with a fief of eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu was Chancellor he followed Wei Xiaokuan in defeating Yu Chi Jiong at Xiangzhou, was given the rank of Upper Opening Master, and made Marquis of Gantang with a fief of eight hundred households.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，進爵為公。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication, his rank was advanced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu received the abdication, his rank was advanced to duke.

sentences.zh: 尋授驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed General of the Swift Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed General of the Swift Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 開皇九年，平陳之役，授行軍總管。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Kaihuang, in the campaign to pacify Chen, he was appointed campaigning commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Kaihuang, during the conquest of Chen, he was appointed campaigning commander.

sentences.zh: 及陳平，晉王廣大獵于蔣山，有猛獸在圍中，眾皆懼。

translations.literal: When Chen was pacified, the Prince of Jin Yang Guang held a great hunt on Mount Jiang; a fierce beast was within the encirclement and all were afraid.
translations.idiomatic: After Chen fell, the Prince of Jin held a great hunt on Mount Jiang; when a fierce beast appeared inside the ring, everyone was afraid.

sentences.zh: 洪馳馬射之，應弦而倒。

translations.literal: Hong galloped and shot it; at the twang of the bowstring it fell.
translations.idiomatic: Hong galloped up and shot it; at the twang of the string the beast fell.

sentences.zh: 陳氏諸將，列觀於側，莫不歎伏焉。

translations.literal: The Chen generals standing in ranks to watch were all amazed and submitted in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: The Chen commanders watching from the side were all struck with wonder.

sentences.zh: 王大喜，賜縑百匹。

translations.literal: The prince was greatly pleased and gave him a hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The prince was delighted and gave him a hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 尋以功加柱國，拜蔣州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon, for merit, he was advanced to Pillar of State and appointed Administrator of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, for his merit, he was advanced to Pillar of State and appointed Administrator of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 數歲，轉廉州刺史。

translations.literal: Several years later he was transferred to Administrator of Lianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was transferred to Administrator of Lianzhou.

sentences.zh: 時突厥屢為邊患，朝廷以洪驍勇，檢校朔州總管事。

translations.literal: At that time the Turks repeatedly troubled the border; the court, because Hong was fierce and brave, made him acting inspector of the affairs of the Commander-in-Chief of Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks were raiding the frontier again and again; because Hong was fierce and bold, the court made him acting inspector of the affairs of the Commander-in-Chief of Shuozhou.

sentences.zh: 尋拜代州總管。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Commander-in-Chief of Daizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Commander-in-Chief of Daizhou.

sentences.zh: 仁壽元年，突厥達頭可汗犯塞，洪率蔚州刺史劉隆、大將軍李藥王拒之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Renshou, the Turk qaghan Tardu invaded the frontier; Hong led the Administrator of Yu prefecture Liu Long and the Grand General Li Yaowang to resist.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Renshou, the Turk qaghan Tardu crossed the border; Hong led the Administrator of Yu Liu Long and the Grand General Li Yaowang to meet him.

sentences.zh: 遇虜于恆安，眾寡不敵，洪四面搏戰，身被重創，將士沮氣。

translations.literal: They met the enemy at Heng'an; their numbers were unequal; Hong fought on all sides, himself suffering grave wounds, and the officers and men lost heart.
translations.idiomatic: They met the enemy at Heng'an; badly outnumbered, Hong fought on every side, took heavy wounds himself, and his troops lost heart.

sentences.zh: 虜悉眾圍之，矢下如雨。

translations.literal: The enemy surrounded them with their full strength; arrows fell like rain.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy closed in with their full strength; arrows fell like rain.

sentences.zh: 洪偽與虜和，圍少解。

translations.literal: Hong pretended to make peace with the enemy and the siege loosened somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: Hong feigned a truce with the enemy, and the encirclement slackened.

sentences.zh: 洪率所領潰圍而出，死者大半，殺虜亦倍。

translations.literal: Hong led his men in breaking out; more than half died, but they also killed twice as many of the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Hong broke out with his command; more than half his men died, yet they killed twice as many of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 洪及藥王除名為民，隆竟坐死。

translations.literal: Hong and Li Yaowang were struck from the rolls and made commoners; Liu Long was put to death for the offense.
translations.idiomatic: Hong and Li Yaowang were removed from office and reduced to commoners; Liu Long was executed.

sentences.zh: 煬帝北巡，至恆安，見白骨被野，以問侍臣。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang toured the north and reached Heng'an, he saw white bones covering the wilds and asked his attendants.
translations.idiomatic: On a northern tour Emperor Yang came to Heng'an, saw white bones strewn across the countryside, and asked his attendants.

sentences.zh: 侍臣曰：「往者韓洪與虜戰處也。

translations.literal: The attendants said: "This is where Han Hong once fought the barbarians."
translations.idiomatic: They said, "This is where Han Hong once fought the barbarians."

sentences.zh: 」帝憫然傷之，收葬骸骨，命五郡沙門為設佛供，拜洪隴西太守。

translations.literal: " The emperor was moved to pity and had the bones gathered and buried, ordered monks of five commanderies to offer Buddhist rites, and appointed Hong Administrator of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Moved to pity, he had the bones gathered and buried, ordered monks from five commanderies to perform Buddhist offerings, and appointed Hong Administrator of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 未幾，硃崖民王萬昌作亂，詔洪擊平之。

translations.literal: Before long the people of Zhuyai, Wang Wanchang, rebelled; an edict ordered Hong to attack and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Wang Wanchang of Zhuyai rebelled; an edict ordered Hong to crush the rising.

sentences.zh: 以功加位金紫光祿大夫，領郡如故。

translations.literal: For merit his rank was advanced to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, while he continued to hold the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was advanced to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon while retaining his prefecture.

sentences.zh: 俄而萬昌弟仲通複叛，又詔洪討平之。

translations.literal: Soon Wanchang's younger brother Zhongtong rebelled again, and Hong was again ordered to pacify him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Wanchang's younger brother Zhongtong rebelled again, and Hong was again ordered to put him down.

sentences.zh: 師未旋，遇疾而卒，時年六十三。

translations.literal: Before the army could return he fell ill and died, aged sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: Before his troops could return he fell ill and died, at the age of sixty-three.

sentences.zh: ○賀若弼

translations.literal: ○ He Ruobi
translations.idiomatic: ○ He Ruobi

sentences.zh: 賀若弼，字輔伯，河南洛陽人也。

translations.literal: He Ruobi, courtesy name Fubo, was a native of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He Ruobi, whose courtesy name was Fubo, came from Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 父敦，以武烈知名，仕周為金州總管，宇文護忌而害之。

translations.literal: His father Dun was famed for martial valor; he served Zhou as Commander-in-Chief of Jinzhou; Yuwen Hu envied and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: His father Dun won fame for martial prowess, served Zhou as Commander-in-Chief of Jinzhou, and was killed by Yuwen Hu out of jealousy.

sentences.zh: 臨刑，呼弼謂之曰：「吾必欲平江南，然此心不果，汝當成吾志。

translations.literal: At execution he called Bi and said to him: "I was determined to pacify the south, yet this heart did not succeed—you must fulfill my aim.
translations.idiomatic: Facing execution he called Bi to him and said, "I was resolved to pacify the south, yet this wish went unfulfilled—you must complete it for me.

sentences.zh: 且吾以舌死，汝不可不思。

translations.literal: Moreover I die for my tongue; you must not fail to reflect on this."
translations.idiomatic: And I die because of my tongue—do not forget that lesson."

sentences.zh: 」因引錐刺弼舌出血，誡以慎口。

translations.literal: " He then took an awl and pierced Bi's tongue until it bled, admonishing him to guard his mouth.
translations.idiomatic: He then drove an awl through Bi's tongue until it bled, warning him to be careful in speech.

sentences.zh: 弼少慷慨有大志，驍勇便弓馬，解屬文，博涉書記，有重名於當世。

translations.literal: Bi in youth was open-handed with great resolve, fierce and skilled at bow and horse, able at linked prose, broadly versed in records, with heavy fame in his age.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Bi was generous and ambitious, fierce and skilled with bow and horse, capable in literary composition, widely read in records, and celebrated in his day.

sentences.zh: 周齊王憲聞而敬之，引為記室。

translations.literal: Prince Xian of Qi Zhou heard and respected him and took him as recorder.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xian of Qi heard of him, admired him, and took him on as recorder.

sentences.zh: 未幾，封當亭縣公，遷小內史。

translations.literal: Before long he was enfeoffed Duke of Dangting county and promoted to Junior Palace Scribe.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was enfeoffed Duke of Dangting and promoted to Junior Palace Scribe.

sentences.zh: 周武帝時，上柱國烏丸軌言於帝曰：「太子非帝王器，臣亦嘗與賀若弼論之。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Wu of Zhou, the Supreme Pillar Wuyan Gui said to the emperor: "The Crown Prince is not material for an emperor; your servant also once discussed this with He Ruobi."
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu of Zhou, the Supreme Pillar Wuyan Gui told the emperor, "The Crown Prince lacks the makings of a ruler; I have discussed this with He Ruobi as well."

sentences.zh: 」帝呼弼問之，弼知太子不可動搖，恐禍及己，詭對曰：「皇太子德業日新，未睹其闕。

translations.literal: " The emperor summoned Bi and asked him; Bi knew the Crown Prince could not be shaken and feared disaster reaching himself, and answered deceitfully: "The Crown Prince's virtue and achievement grow daily; I have not seen his faults."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Bi and questioned him; knowing the Crown Prince could not be moved and fearing harm to himself, Bi answered evasively, "The Crown Prince's virtue and accomplishments improve daily; I have seen no fault in him."

sentences.zh: 」帝默然。

translations.literal: " The emperor was silent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said nothing.

sentences.zh: 弼既退，軌讓其背己，弼曰：「君不密則失臣，臣不密則失身，所以不敢輕議也。

translations.literal: When Bi withdrew, Gui reproached him for betraying him; Bi said: "If the lord is not discreet he loses his minister; if the minister is not discreet he loses his person—therefore I dared not speak lightly."
translations.idiomatic: After Bi withdrew, Gui reproached him for betraying him; Bi said, "When the ruler is not discreet he loses his minister; when the minister is not discreet he loses his life—that is why I dared not speak lightly."

sentences.zh: 」及宣帝嗣位，軌竟見誅，弼乃獲免。

translations.literal: " When Emperor Xuan succeeded, Gui was indeed executed, and Bi thus escaped.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, Gui was indeed executed, and Bi thus escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 尋與韋孝寬伐陳，攻拔數十城，弼計居多。

translations.literal: Soon he followed Wei Xiaokuan in attacking Chen and captured several tens of cities; Bi's plans were mostly foremost.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he followed Wei Xiaokuan in campaigning against Chen and took dozens of cities; Bi's stratagems led the way.

sentences.zh: 拜夀州刺史，改封襄邑縣公。

translations.literal: He was appointed Administrator of Shouzhou and his fief was changed to Duke of Xiangyi county.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Administrator of Shouzhou and his fief was changed to Duke of Xiangyi.

sentences.zh: 高祖為丞相，尉迥作亂鄴城，恐弼為變，遣長孫平馳驛代之。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was Chancellor, Yu Chi Jiong rebelled at Ye; fearing Bi might change sides, he sent Zhangsun Ping by post relay to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu was Chancellor, Yu Chi Jiong rebelled at Ye; fearing Bi might turn traitor, he sent Zhangsun Ping by urgent relay to replace him.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，陰有並江南之志，訪可任者。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication, he secretly cherished the aim of uniting with the south and asked who could be entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne he quietly aimed to absorb the south and asked whom he could entrust.

sentences.zh: 高熲曰：「朝臣之內，文武才幹，無若賀若弼者。

translations.literal: Gao Jiong said: "Among the court ministers in civil and military talent there is none like He Ruobi."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jiong said, "Among the ministers at court, none matches He Ruobi in civil and military talent."

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「公得之矣。

translations.literal: " Gaozu said: "You have found the man."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "You have found the man."

sentences.zh: 」於是拜弼為吳州總管，委以平陳之事，弼忻然以為己任。

translations.literal: " He then appointed Bi Commander-in-Chief of Wuzhou and entrusted him with pacifying Chen; Bi gladly took it as his own charge.
translations.idiomatic: He then appointed Bi Commander-in-Chief of Wuzhou and entrusted him with the conquest of Chen; Bi gladly made it his own mission.

sentences.zh: 與壽州總管源雄並為重鎮。

translations.literal: He and the Commander-in-Chief of Shouzhou Yuan Xiong were together key strongholds.
translations.idiomatic: He and Yuan Xiong, Commander-in-Chief of Shouzhou, formed paired bastions of strength.

sentences.zh: 弼遺雄詩曰：「交河驃騎幕，合浦伏波營，勿使騏驎上，無我二人名。」

translations.literal: Bi sent Xiong a poem: "The swift-cavalry camp at Jiaohe, the Fubo camp at Hepu—do not let the qilin mount up without our two names upon it."
translations.idiomatic: Bi sent Xiong a poem: "The swift-cavalry camp at Jiaohe, the Fubo camp at Hepu—let no qilin charge heavenward without our two names upon it."

sentences.zh: 獻取陳十策，上稱善，賜以寶刀。

translations.literal: He presented ten stratagems for taking Chen; the emperor praised them and gave him a precious saber.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted ten stratagems for taking Chen; the emperor praised them and gave him a precious saber.

sentences.zh: 開皇九年，大舉伐陳，以弼為行軍總管。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Kaihuang the great campaign against Chen was launched; Bi was made campaigning commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Kaihuang the great assault on Chen was mounted; Bi was made campaigning commander.

sentences.zh: 將渡江，酹酒而咒曰：「弼親承廟略，遠振國威，伐罪吊民，除凶翦暴，上天長江，鑒其若此。

translations.literal: About to cross the river, he poured a libation and swore: "Bi personally receives the temple strategy, displays the state's might afar, punishes crime and comforts the people, removes the vicious and cuts down the violent—Heaven and the Long River, witness this!"
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to cross the Yangtze he poured a libation and swore, "Bi personally carries out the court's plan, displays our might afar, punishes the guilty and comforts the people, uproots cruelty and violence—Heaven and the Long River, bear witness!"

sentences.zh: 如便福善禍淫，大軍利涉；

translations.literal: If fortune favors the good and punishes the evil, the great army will cross in safety;
translations.idiomatic: If Heaven favors the good and punishes evil, the great army will cross safely;

sentences.zh: 如事有乖違，得葬江魚腹中，死且不恨。

translations.literal: if things go against this, let me be buried in the bellies of the river fish—I shall die without regret."
translations.idiomatic: if things go otherwise, let me be buried in the bellies of the river fish—I shall die without regret."

sentences.zh: 」先是，弼請緣江防人每交代之際，必集曆陽。

translations.literal: " Earlier Bi had requested that whenever the river guards changed shifts they must assemble at Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Bi had arranged that whenever the river guards changed shifts they must assemble at Liyang.

sentences.zh: 於是大列旗幟，營幕被野。

translations.literal: Thereupon he arrayed banners on a great scale and tents covered the wilds.
translations.idiomatic: There he arrayed banners on a vast scale until camp pavilions covered the countryside.

sentences.zh: 陳人以為大兵至，悉發國中士馬。

translations.literal: The Chen thought a great army had come and mobilized all the troops and horses in the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The Chen believed a great army had arrived and mobilized every soldier and horse in the realm.

sentences.zh: 既知防人交代，其眾複散。

translations.literal: When they learned it was only the guard changing shifts, the masses dispersed again.
translations.idiomatic: When they learned it was only a guard rotation, the forces dispersed again.

sentences.zh: 後以為常，不復設備。

translations.literal: Later this became routine and they no longer made preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward they took it as routine and no longer kept watch.

sentences.zh: 及此，弼以大軍濟江，陳人弗之覺也。

translations.literal: At this time Bi crossed the great army over the river and the Chen did not perceive it.
translations.idiomatic: This time Bi ferried the great army across the river, and the Chen never noticed.

sentences.zh: 襲陳南徐州，拔之，執其刺史黃恪。

translations.literal: He struck Chen's Southern Xuzhou and took it, seizing its Administrator Huang Ke.
translations.idiomatic: He struck Chen Southern Xuzhou, captured it, and seized its Administrator Huang Ke.

sentences.zh: 軍令嚴肅，秋毫不犯。

translations.literal: Army orders were strict; not a hair was harmed.
translations.idiomatic: His army orders were severe; not a hair of the people was touched.

sentences.zh: 有軍士于民間沽酒者，弼立斬之。

translations.literal: A soldier who bought wine among the people—Bi immediately beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: When a soldier bought wine from civilians, Bi had him beheaded on the spot.

sentences.zh: 進屯蔣山之白土岡，陳將魯達、周智安、任蠻奴、田瑞、樊毅、孔范、蕭摩訶等以勁兵拒戰。

translations.literal: Advancing he encamped at Baitu Hill on Mount Jiang; the Chen generals Lu Da, Zhou Zhi'an, Ren Mannu, Tian Rui, Fan Yi, Kong Fan, Xiao Mohe and others with crack troops resisted.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to Baitu Hill on Mount Jiang; the Chen commanders Lu Da, Zhou Zhi'an, Ren Mannu, Tian Rui, Fan Yi, Kong Fan, Xiao Mohe, and others met him with elite troops.

sentences.zh: 田瑞先犯弼軍，弼擊走之。

translations.literal: Tian Rui first attacked Bi's army; Bi struck and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Rui attacked first; Bi beat him back.

sentences.zh: 魯達等相繼遞進，弼軍屢卻。

translations.literal: Lu Da and the others advanced in succession; Bi's army repeatedly gave ground.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Da and the others pressed forward in turn; Bi's army fell back again and again.

sentences.zh: 弼揣知其驕，士卒且惰，於是督厲將士，殊死戰，遂大破之。

translations.literal: Bi judged them arrogant and the soldiers slack; he then urged the officers and men to fight to the death and greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Bi judged them arrogant and his own men slack; he then drove his troops to fight to the death and routed them utterly.

sentences.zh: 麾下開府員明擒摩訶至，弼命左右牽斬之。

translations.literal: His subordinate the Opening Master Yuan Ming brought Mohe captive; Bi ordered attendants to drag him out for execution.
translations.idiomatic: His subordinate the Opening Master Yuan Ming brought Mohe in bonds; Bi ordered his men to drag him out for execution.

sentences.zh: 摩訶顏色自若，弼釋而禮之。

translations.literal: Mohe's countenance was calm as ever; Bi released him and treated him with courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Mohe's face remained calm; Bi released him and treated him with courtesy.

sentences.zh: 從北掖門而入。

translations.literal: He entered through the North Yeta Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He entered through the North Yeta Gate.

sentences.zh: 時韓擒虎已執陳叔寶，弼至，呼叔寶視之。

translations.literal: At the time Han Qinhu had already seized Chen Shubao; when Bi arrived he called Shubao forth to look at him.
translations.idiomatic: By then Han Qinhu had already taken Chen Shubao prisoner; when Bi arrived he had Shubao brought out before him.

sentences.zh: 叔寶惶懼流汗，股忄栗再拜。

translations.literal: Shubao was fearful, sweating, his legs trembling as he bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: Shubao was terrified, sweat streaming down him, his legs shaking as he bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 弼謂之曰：「小國之君，當大國卿，拜，禮也。

translations.literal: Bi said to him: "A ruler of a small state meeting a minister of a great state—bowing is the rite.
translations.idiomatic: Bi told him, "A ruler of a small state who meets a minister of a great power bows—that is proper ritual.

sentences.zh: 入朝不失作歸命侯，無勞恐懼。

translations.literal: Going to court you will not lose the rank of Marquis Who Surrendered—do not trouble yourself with fear."
translations.idiomatic: When you go to court you will still be made Marquis Who Surrendered—there is no need for such fear."

sentences.zh: 」既而弼恚恨不獲叔寶，功在韓擒虎之後，於是與擒虎相詢，挺刃而出。

translations.literal: " Then Bi resented that he had not captured Shubao himself and that his merit stood behind Han Qinhu's; he and Qinhu confronted each other and drew blades.
translations.idiomatic: Then Bi, resentful that he had not taken Shubao himself and that his merit ranked behind Qinhu's, faced Qinhu and drew his blade.

sentences.zh: 上聞弼有功，大悅，下詔褒揚，語在《韓擒虎傳》。

translations.literal: The emperor heard that Bi had merit and was greatly pleased; he issued an edict of praise—the words are in the biography of Han Qinhu.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of Bi's merit he was greatly pleased and issued an edict of praise—the text appears in the biography of Han Qinhu.

sentences.zh: 晉王以弼先期決戰，違軍命，於是以弼屬吏。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin, because Bi had given battle ahead of schedule in violation of army orders, handed Bi over to the legal officers.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin, because Bi had fought ahead of schedule in violation of orders, handed him over to the legal officers.

sentences.zh: 上驛召之，及見，迎勞曰：」克定三吳，公之功也。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned him by post relay; when he saw him he welcomed and comforted him, saying: "Pacifying the Three Wu is your merit."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned him by urgent relay; when they met he welcomed and praised him, saying, "Pacifying the Three Wu is your achievement."

sentences.zh: 「命登禦坐，賜物八千段，加位上柱國，進爵宋國公，真食襄邑三千戶，加以寶劍、寶帶、金甕、金盤各一，並雉尾扇、曲蓋，雜彩二千段，女樂二部，又賜陳叔寶妹為妾。

translations.literal: He ordered him to ascend the imperial seat and gave eight thousand bolts of goods, advanced him to Supreme Pillar of State, promoted him to Duke of Song with a true fief of three thousand households at Xiangyi, and moreover gave one each of precious saber, precious belt, golden jar, and golden platter, together with peacock-tail fans and curved canopy, two thousand bolts of mixed silks, two companies of female musicians, and also gave him Chen Shubao's younger sister as concubine.
translations.idiomatic: He had him sit on the imperial couch, gave eight thousand bolts of goods, advanced him to Supreme Pillar of State, promoted him to Duke of Song with a true fief of three thousand households at Xiangyi, and also bestowed a precious saber, belt, golden jar, and golden platter, peacock-tail fans and a curved canopy, two thousand bolts of mixed silks, two troupes of female musicians, and Chen Shubao's younger sister as a concubine.

sentences.zh: 拜右領軍大將軍，尋轉右武候大將軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed General of the Right Palace Guard and soon transferred to General of the Right Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General of the Right Palace Guard and soon transferred to General of the Right Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 弼時貴盛，位望隆重，其兄隆為武都郡公，弟東為萬榮郡公，並刺史、列將。

translations.literal: At that time Bi was at the height of honor; his rank and renown were weighty; his elder brother Long was Duke of Wudu commandery and his younger brother Dong Duke of Wanrong commandery—both prefects and ranked generals.
translations.idiomatic: Bi was then at the height of power; his elder brother Long was Duke of Wudu and his younger brother Dong Duke of Wanrong—both prefects and field commanders.

sentences.zh: 弼家珍玩不可勝計，婢妾曳綺羅者數百，時人榮之。

translations.literal: Bi's house held curios beyond counting; several hundred concubines trailed in brocade and gauze—men of the time envied him.
translations.idiomatic: His house held treasures beyond counting; hundreds of concubines trailed silk and gauze—men of the age envied him.

sentences.zh: 弼自謂功名出朝臣之右，每以宰相自許。

translations.literal: Bi considered his merit and fame above the court ministers and constantly styled himself a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Bi believed his merit outshone the ministers and constantly spoke of himself as fit for the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 既而楊素為右僕射，弼仍為將軍，甚不平，形於言色，由是免官，弼怨望愈甚。

translations.literal: Soon Yang Su became Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs while Bi remained a general; he was very discontent and showed it in speech and face; for this he was dismissed from office and his resentment grew.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Su became Right Vice Director while Bi remained a mere general, he was deeply discontent, showed it openly, and was dismissed; his resentment only deepened.

sentences.zh: 後數年，下弼獄，上謂之曰：「我以高熲、楊素為宰相，汝每倡言，雲此二人惟堪啖飯耳，是何意也？

translations.literal: Several years later Bi was imprisoned; the emperor said to him: "I made Gao Jiong and Yang Su chancellors; you constantly proclaimed that these two men were fit only to eat rice—what did you mean?"
translations.idiomatic: Years later Bi was thrown into prison; the emperor said to him, "I made Gao Jiong and Yang Su my chancellors, yet you kept saying those two were fit only to eat rice—what did you mean by that?"

sentences.zh: 」弼曰：「熲，臣之故人，素，臣之舅子，臣並知其為人，誠有此語。

translations.literal: " Bi said: "Jiong is your servant's old friend; Su is your servant's nephew by marriage; your servant knows both their characters—those words were indeed spoken."
translations.idiomatic: Bi answered, "Jiong is an old friend of mine and Su is my nephew by marriage; I know them both well—those words were truly spoken."

sentences.zh: 」公卿奏弼怨望，罪當死。

translations.literal: " The ministers memorialized that Bi harbored resentment and the crime merited death.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers memorialized that Bi harbored resentment and deserved death.

sentences.zh: 上惜其功，於是除名為民。

translations.literal: The emperor cherished his merit and therefore struck his name from the rolls and made him a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor valued his past service and therefore struck his name from the rolls and reduced him to a commoner.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，複其爵位。

translations.literal: After more than a year his rank and title were restored.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year his rank and title were restored.

sentences.zh: 上亦忌之，不復任使，然每宴賜，遇之甚厚。

translations.literal: The emperor also grew wary of him and no longer employed him, yet whenever he feasted and gave gifts he treated him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also grew wary and no longer gave him office, yet at every feast and gift he treated him generously.

sentences.zh: 開皇十九年，上幸仁壽宮，宴王公，詔弼為五言詩，詞意憤怨，帝覽而容之。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Kaihuang the emperor visited Renshou Palace and feasted the princes and dukes; he ordered Bi to compose a pentasyllabic poem—the words were resentful, yet the emperor read it and bore with him.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year of Kaihuang the emperor visited Renshou Palace and feasted the princes and dukes; he ordered Bi to compose a pentasyllabic poem—its tone was bitter, yet the emperor read it and indulged him.

sentences.zh: 嘗遇突厥入朝，上賜之射，突厥一發中的。

translations.literal: Once when Turks came to court the emperor granted them an archery contest; a Turk hit the target with one shot.
translations.idiomatic: Once when Turks came to court the emperor granted them a shooting match; a Turk hit the target on his first shot.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「非賀若弼無能當此。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Only He Ruobi can meet this."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Only He Ruobi can answer this."

sentences.zh: 」於是命弼。

translations.literal: " He then ordered Bi.
translations.idiomatic: He then summoned Bi.

sentences.zh: 弼再拜祝曰：「臣若赤誠奉國者，當一發破的。

translations.literal: Bi bowed twice and prayed: "If your servant is loyal and devoted to the state, let this one shot strike the mark.
translations.idiomatic: Bi bowed twice and prayed, "If I am loyal and devoted to the state, let this one shot strike home.

sentences.zh: 如其不然，發不中也。

translations.literal: If not, let the shot miss."
translations.idiomatic: If not, let it miss."

sentences.zh: 」既射，一發而中。

translations.literal: " He shot and with one arrow hit.
translations.idiomatic: He shot and hit with a single arrow.

sentences.zh: 上大悅，顧謂突厥曰：「此人天賜我也！」

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and turning to the Turks said: "This man Heaven gave to me!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and told the Turks, "Heaven gave me this man!"

sentences.zh: 煬帝之在東宮，嘗謂弼曰：「楊素、韓擒虎、史萬歲三人，俱稱良將，優劣如何？

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang was Eastern Heir, he once said to Bi: "Yang Su, Han Qinhu, and Shi Wansui are all called fine generals—how do they rank in excellence?"
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang was crown prince he once asked Bi, "Yang Su, Han Qinhu, and Shi Wansui are all called fine generals—how do they compare?"

sentences.zh: 」弼曰：「楊素是猛將，非謀將；

translations.literal: " Bi said: "Yang Su is a fierce general, not a strategist;
translations.idiomatic: Bi said, "Yang Su is a fierce fighter, not a strategist;

sentences.zh: 韓擒虎是鬥將，非領將；

translations.literal: Han Qinhu is a duelist, not a commander;
translations.idiomatic: Han Qinhu is a duelist, not a commander;

sentences.zh: 史萬歲是騎將，非大將。

translations.literal: Shi Wansui is a cavalry general, not a great marshal."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Wansui is a cavalry leader, not a supreme commander."

sentences.zh: 」太子曰：「然則大將誰也？

translations.literal: " The Crown Prince said: "Then who is the great marshal?"
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince asked, "Then who is the great marshal?"

sentences.zh: 」弼拜曰：「唯殿下所擇。

translations.literal: " Bi bowed and said: "Only as Your Highness chooses."
translations.idiomatic: Bi bowed and said, "Whomever Your Highness selects."

sentences.zh: 」弼意自許為大將。

translations.literal: " Bi in his heart styled himself the great marshal.
translations.idiomatic: In his heart Bi meant himself as the great marshal.

sentences.zh: 及煬帝嗣位，尤被疏忌。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded, he was especially kept at a distance and suspected.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang took the throne, Bi was kept at an even greater distance and viewed with suspicion.

sentences.zh: 大業三年，從駕北巡，至榆林。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daye he followed the imperial tour north to Yulin.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Daye he accompanied the emperor on the northern tour as far as Yulin.

sentences.zh: 帝時為大帳，其下可坐數千人，召突厥啟民可汗饗之。

translations.literal: The emperor then had a great tent under which several thousand could sit, and summoned the Turk qaghan Qimin for a feast.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pitched a great tent that could seat thousands and summoned the Turk qaghan Qimin to a feast.

sentences.zh: 弼以為大侈，與高熲、宇文弼等私議得失，為人所奏，竟坐誅，時年六十四。

translations.literal: Bi considered it extravagantly grand; he privately discussed its faults with Gao Jiong, Yuwen Bi and others; someone reported them and he was finally executed for the offense, aged sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Bi judged the display extravagantly grand and privately discussed its faults with Gao Jiong, Yuwen Bi, and others; someone denounced them and he was executed, aged sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 妻子為官奴婢，群從徙邊。

translations.literal: His wife and children were made government slave-girls; his clansmen were banished to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: His wife and children were made government slaves; his kinsmen were exiled to the borderlands.

sentences.zh: 子懷亮，慷慨有父風，以柱國世子拜儀同三司。

translations.literal: His son Huailiang was open-handed with his father's manner; as heir of a Pillar of State he was appointed Yitong Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huailiang was generous and bold like his father; as heir of a Pillar of State he was appointed Yitong Third Rank.

sentences.zh: 坐弼為奴，俄亦誅死。

translations.literal: Because of Bi's punishment as a slave he too was soon executed.
translations.idiomatic: Because of Bi's disgrace he too was soon put to death.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：夫天地未泰，聖哲啟其機；

translations.literal: The historiographer says: When heaven and earth are not at peace, sages and worthies open the opportunity;
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: When heaven and earth are not yet at peace, sages open the way forward;

sentences.zh: 疆埸尚梗，爪牙宣其力。

translations.literal: when the frontier is still blocked, talons and fangs display their strength.
translations.idiomatic: when the frontiers still bar the way, warriors display their strength.

sentences.zh: 周之方、邵，漢室韓、彭，代有其人，非一時也。

translations.literal: Fang and Shao of Zhou, Han and Peng of the Han house—each age has such men; it is not of one time alone.
translations.idiomatic: Fang and Shao of Zhou, Han Xin and Peng Yue of Han—every age produces such men; it is never a matter of one moment alone.

sentences.zh: 自晉衰微，中原幅裂，區宇分隔，將三百年。

translations.literal: From the decline of Jin the central plains were torn apart; the realm was divided—for nearly three hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: From Jin's decline the central plains were torn asunder; the realm lay divided for nearly three hundred years.

sentences.zh: 陳氏憑長江之地險，恃金陵之餘氣，以為天限南北，人莫能窺。

translations.literal: The Chen relied on the Yangtze's strategic terrain and trusted in Jinling's remaining vigor, thinking heaven barred north and south and no man could peer across.
translations.idiomatic: The Chen trusted the Yangtze's natural barrier and Jinling's lingering strength, believing heaven itself divided north from south so that none could cross.

sentences.zh: 高祖爰應千齡，將一函夏。

translations.literal: Gaozu then answered the call of a thousand years and was about to unite all within the seas.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu then answered the summons of the age and set out to unite the realm within the four seas.

sentences.zh: 賀若弼慷慨，申必取之長策，韓擒虎奮發，賈餘勇以爭先，勢甚疾雷，鋒逾駭電。

translations.literal: He Ruobi, open-handed and bold, set forth the long strategy that must take it; Han Qinhu roused himself and sold his remaining courage to strive ahead—momentum like swift thunder, edge surpassing startled lightning.
translations.idiomatic: He Ruobi, bold and generous, laid out the strategy that had to prevail; Han Qinhu threw himself forward and spent his last strength to race ahead—momentum like thunder, blades swifter than lightning.

sentences.zh: 隋氏自此一戎，威加四海。

translations.literal: From this one campaign the Sui house displayed might across the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: With this single campaign the house of Sui made its might felt across the four seas.

sentences.zh: 稽諸天道，或時有廢興，考之人謀，實二臣之力。

translations.literal: Examining it against the way of heaven, rise and fall come in their seasons; weighing human design, it was truly the power of these two ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Measured against heaven's way, fortune rises and falls in its seasons; measured by human counsel, it was truly the work of these two ministers.

sentences.zh: 其俶儻英略，賀若居多，武毅威雄，韓擒虎稱重。

translations.literal: In bold vision and heroic design He Ruo predominates; in martial sternness and awe-inspiring might Han Qinhu carries weight.
translations.idiomatic: In daring strategy and heroic design He Ruo predominates; in martial sternness and commanding presence Han Qinhu carries the greater weight.

sentences.zh: 方于晉之王、杜，勳庸綽有餘地。

translations.literal: Compared with Wang and Du of Jin, their merit still leaves room beyond.
translations.idiomatic: Even beside Wang Jun and Du Yu of Jin, their achievements still stand taller.

sentences.zh: 然賀若功成名立，矜伐不已，竟顛殞於非命，亦不密以失身。

translations.literal: Yet He Ruo, merit and fame established, boasted without end and finally fell in an untimely death—also because he was not discreet and lost his person.
translations.idiomatic: Yet He Ruo, once merit and fame were won, kept boasting without end and finally died before his time—having failed, too, to guard his tongue and preserve himself.

sentences.zh: 若念父臨終之言，必不及於斯禍矣。

translations.literal: Had he kept his father's words at the end, he would surely not have reached this calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Had he remembered his father's dying words, he would never have come to this ruin.

sentences.zh: 韓擒虎累世將家，威聲動俗，敵國既破，名遂身全，幸也。

translations.literal: Han Qinhu, a general's house for generations, prestige shaking the age; the enemy state once broken, fame complete and person preserved—fortunate indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qinhu came from generations of commanders, his renown shaking the age; once the enemy state fell, he kept both fame and life—fortunate indeed.

sentences.zh: 廣陵、甘棠，鹹有武藝，驍雄膽略，並為當時所推，赳赳干城，難兄難弟矣。

translations.literal: Guangling and Gantang both had martial arts; fierce valor and daring stratagem were alike pushed by the age—stalwart bulwarks of the realm, brothers hard to tell apart.
translations.idiomatic: Guangling and Gantang both possessed martial skill; fierce courage and daring strategy alike won the esteem of the age—stalwart shields of the state, brothers matched in glory.
